requirements.name: One filter drives every dashboard
requirements.why: "this view is powerful because it lets us filter specifically and then see the analysis on all of the views"; dataset first, split across every dataset ticked.
requirements.passCondition: A pick in the rail (dataset, split, kind, a trajectory) changes what every dashboard shows, honestly labelled as the subset, and the filter is always visible or one glance away.

anchors.1: Filters are per dashboard, or a dashboard ignores the rail.
anchors.3: Every dashboard follows the rail, but the current filter is hard to see from a dashboard, or some figures don't recount.
anchors.5: Every dashboard recounts from the rail, says it is a subset, and the active filter stays legible on every tab.

requirements.name: Drops into any app
requirements.why: "I want the viewer to be a bit more compact … so it can drop into anything"; tabs at the top top make it "harder to put it in another app".
requirements.passCondition: The same component works full page and inside a host's 1000 × 680 slot, owns no page-level chrome, and stays usable at that size.

anchors.1: Needs the whole page (page-top tabs, fixed layers) or breaks in the slot.
anchors.3: Fits the slot but cramped: the rail or the figures become hard to use.
anchors.5: Fits the slot comfortably (the rail folds or narrows, figures re-fit), with nothing outside it.

requirements.name: Switching dashboards feels like tabs
requirements.why: "I do like kinda a more Tab feeling view though for those top tabs, because … we are filtering data and then switching between dashboards almost".
requirements.passCondition: One click switches the dashboard, the set of dashboards is visible at once, and the filter and scroll context survive the switch.

anchors.1: Dashboards are separate pages or buried in a menu.
anchors.3: Switching works but the dashboards' names aren't all visible, or switching loses context.
anchors.5: All dashboards visible as one row or list, one click, nothing lost.

requirements.name: A reusable data-ui pattern
requirements.why: "this general pattern … should be supported in data-ui … this will happen again and again!"
requirements.passCondition: The pattern is expressed in data-ui's grammar (.base + elements) with little host code, and a second app could use it unchanged.

anchors.1: Mostly host code; another app would copy and adapt it.
anchors.3: Partly data-ui, partly host glue that each app would redo.
anchors.5: A small, named data-ui addition (an element or .base keys) that any app drops in with its own rows and dashboards.

requirements.name: Within-dashboard filters stay local; settings set once
requirements.why: "We also need like further filtering within the page though... For example for the joints"; colours behind a gear (round 2).
requirements.passCondition: A dashboard's own controls (the joint picker) show only there; component-wide settings live behind one gear inside the component.

anchors.1: Local and global controls mixed into one strip everywhere.
anchors.3: Mostly scoped, with a stray control.
anchors.5: Every control acts on what's in view; one gear for the rest.

requirements.name: Across datasets and within one
requirements.why: "So 1 is across datasets, 2 is within a particular dataset. now I want to be able to filter for particular trajectories".
requirements.passCondition: You can compare datasets (which dataset covers what) and narrow to particular trajectories inside one, in the same component.

anchors.3: Both work, but comparing datasets means flipping filters back and forth.
anchors.5: Datasets are distinguishable at a glance (colour or side by side), and narrowing to trajectories is one step.

hardGates.name: Dataset first; one dataset leaves its trajectories
